brewing.notes: A common starting point for herbal infusions: boiling water, about five minutes.

description:
A large-leaf holly kuding from a tree-form plant, carrying a national geographical indication for Chengmai County, Hainan. It differs from the spiny holly kuding of Yunnan, Guizhou and Sichuan.

Brew it as you would other herbal infusions. If the plant is new to you, check that it is safe for you first, especially when pregnant or on medication.
history: Its gardens lie in misty high ground on nutrient-rich red soil. It has picked up the popular nicknames longevity tea and beauty tea. Little more is documented about it.
processing: Dried plant material, as with most herbal infusions.
harvest_season: Depends on the plant and the place.
appearance_dry: Thick, soft leaf rolled into tight, glossy strips.
appearance_liquor: Green with a yellow cast, clear and bright.
taste_profile: Fresh and strongly aromatic, and it stands up to many infusions.
vintage_note: Herbal infusions are not sold by vintage: buy recent stock and use it within a year or so.
